second person and a duplicate log.

lore.title: A Route Is a Person
pages: The courier path on the signal map includes a blank for the duty
name. Dot added it after noticing every old map treated messages as
if they moved themselves. Moxie filled her name in large letters and
left room for whoever covers her lunch.

lore.title: The Plain Lens
pages: The plain lantern lens costs less than the colored set. The clerk
chose it because a signal should be readable without naming colors.
The unused lenses decorate the tea shelf. Their beauty has found a
job that does not carry an alarm.

lore.title: The Kept Log
pages: The clerk could have discarded the failure log when nobody asked for
it. Instead she copied the fading entries each spring and kept the
original dry. She does not call this hope. She calls it records
care, then offers Dot the good pencil.

lore.title: The Small Sound
pages: A notice asks visitors to listen for changes rather than loudness.
The turbine was designed to run quietly. The opening committee once
requested a dramatic startup noise. A builder suggested paying the
band instead. The band invoice is clipped behind the notice.

lore.title: A Door Beside a Door
pages: The bypass has a plain handle and a clear label. Its designer wrote
that the best backup is one a tired person can find. No hidden
panel, special key riddle, or proud maker mark blocks access. The
proud work is making the ordinary route obvious.

lore.title: The Margin
pages: The grid plan leaves spare capacity marked in pencil. Slush first
called it unused value. Rivet called it room for a fault. The pencil
note now says both, with enough space underneath to record what
happens. Neither has erased the other person's handwriting.

lore.title: The Next Morning
pages: The festival checklist ends after decorations, music, and food with
a separate page: Tomorrow. It names cleaning duties, the first
inspection, and who answers the desk. Pip drew a sun beside that
heading. A festival that leaves a working morning is his favorite
kind.

warmth: The first upgrades reach the clinic, then the drafty homes on the
sheltered circuit. A nurse reports that patients have stopped
wearing their outdoor coats in bed. Pip pins that sentence above the
garage desk. It is better than his speech. Moxie carries a repair
note from a resident who has also packed biscuits. Rivet logs the
note before opening the tin. Dot checks the first week of readings
and finds a small fault, reported early and fixed without a citywide
stop. Slush lends his roof crew and receives an ordinary invoice
marked paid. He looks almost disappointed that nobody wants a
portrait of him holding a hammer. Nib offers him a biscuit instead.
There is still work to do, and you can keep exploring, taking jobs,
or making another property worth coming home to. For tonight, people
have taken their coats off. The city has given them a reason to
industry: The first upgrades warm the repair shops and the training benches.
The new wage board includes paid learning time and names the person
who checks each task. Rivet takes down a heroic poster to make room
for it. Moxie delivers a replacement gear on a route with a real
backup, then spends her break teaching a new courier the address
cards. Dot leads the shutdown test without asking someone else to
read her results aloud. Slush opens his yard for tool training and
discovers that people respect a useful landlord even when his name
is not on the gate. Nib advertises the work honestly: paid,
practical, occasionally oily. The machines have not solved every
problem. They have made repair work possible, and the wages help
people choose what comes next. The city remains open for your own
jobs, properties, and plans. At dusk, a shop whistle sounds once,
exactly when the posted shift ends.
commons: The first upgrades warm the shared halls, public kitchens, and
meeting rooms. Nib posts the opening hours beside the cleaning
duties in print equally large. The first gathering is a soup
exchange. Nobody can agree which soup won, so the clerk suggests
eating the evidence. Moxie adds the halls to a written courier rota.
Rivet teaches a small repair class at a table protected by an
extremely ugly cloth. Dot explains the signal map to residents who
now know whom to ask when a reply fails. Slush lends the lodge hall
on the same posted terms as everyone else. He still carries his
silver umbrella, but has learned to leave it in the common rack. You
can return to free exploration, optional jobs, and properties of
your own. The network has not made everyone agree. It has given them
somewhere warm to work out the disagreement, with spare chairs and
an honest plan for the morning.
